messages.author: 8fbbf490c07a1909
messages.subject: Adjusted angle zig zag error
parts:
Hi all,

I am having an issue that has been raised a couple of times on this forum over the  years.  I’m investigating a few different designs for a program we’re involved in, and the equal-angle and equal-spaced zig zag designs both run fine.  When I try an adjusted angle zig zag, however, I get multiple errors of the following type, and no results:

**Error: Problems generating the adjusted angle zigzag sampler. Too little effort for the survey region height of XXX

I am running Distance 6.2.  I have tried solving the problem – as prompted by Distance – by increasing the survey effort and adjusting the angle (there is only one stratum). 

For some background, this is what I found: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/too$20little$20effort$20for$20the$20survey$20region/distance-sampling/pc0eHrDlNGc/OJcSBbIur-8J

Like Philippe, I note that a design layer is created (despite not showing in the results) and I’m able to add it to a map.  However, I’m not able to estimate probability of coverage using the design (it generates the same errors). 

Any ideas?

Stewart

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Adjusted angle zig zag error
parts:
Stewart:

Thanks for digging back into the email list archives before writing to the list.  I am afraid we have not made any progress on the adjusted angle sawtooth design bug in the Survey Design Engine since the earlier report from 2010.  You'll need to content yourself with designs produced by the equal-spaced sawtooth (that has better properties than the equal-angle sawtooth).
